- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for the next 2–3 periods.
- If model forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias — adjust downward by 1–2% for next period.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is mixed or trending downward, model often fails to capture early decline; add a “sentiment-weighted decay” — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment day.
- If model forecast is > 10% above true outcome in first 5–7 days, apply “early overshoot correction” — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 periods.
